questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your traineeship destination (city/region)? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available at your traineeship destination (organization/city/region)? *
questions.answer: There are student nations that sometimes have activities and clubs going on. There was also May Day celebrations and Christmas tree light ups, and Lucia. Another exciting thing is Valborg which happens in April. On Facebook there are also often events and activities posted, including things happening at the Church.

questions.question: Which non-academic activities would you recommend to future trainees visiting the same destination (organization/city/region)? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend attending a Lucia celebration. This happens around Christmas time and there is usually a choir and it's quite nice. I would also recommend getting involved in Valborg. This was a fun party that happens through the whole city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting trainees see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's very nice to bike to the city centre to walk around. There are also many nice parks around the city. You can also do day trips to places in Skane like Malmo, or when the weather gets warmer to go to Lomma beach.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your trainee host? *
questions.answer: It was not too difficult, I knew them already.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of the destination (city/country)? *
questions.answer: This was not too difficult either, Sweden and Denmark are similar culturally.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with locals? *
questions.answer: Join clubs, like a running club, or take the opportunity to interact with colleagues in the corridor. It's good to build familiarity.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it too challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the politeness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going on a traineeship to the same city/region? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure you start looking for a place a few months in advance, especially if you are starting after summer. There will be other new students starting and it could be difficult when you are competing for a spot.

2. Of course in Denmark many people bike as well, but you should definitely have a bike in Lund! It is the easiest and cheapest way to get around and the city is quite small. There are many second hand shops to get a bike, but still invest in a good one, it can be sold later when you leave.

3. If you do intend to travel around Skane, get the Skanetrafiken app. The ticket prices are better there, and when you return to Denmark then it will be priced at the Swedish krone.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future traineeship students? *

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your traineeship experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of the traineeship was being part of novel interdisciplinary research on a project that I feel very invested in and to be with a lab group that I feel incredibly supported by.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the traineeship? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge has been the workload, but it was also to be expected since it is part of my thesis project.
